title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for left-sided hemiparesis.

HPI
Pt is a 61 y/o male presenting for f/u of residual left-sided hemiparesis following a previous ischemic stroke. Pt reports stable functional status. He notes some difficulty with fine motor tasks, but continues to be left-handed. No new complaints or worsening of symptoms reported since last visit.

Medication List
1. Lisinopril 10mg QD
2. Atorvastatin 20mg QD
3. Aspirin 81mg QD

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented x3.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Extremities: Notable for left hemiparesis. Strength is 4/5 in the left upper and lower extremities. Sensation intact.
Neuro: Cranial nerves II-XII intact.

Assessment
1. Residual left-sided hemiparesis secondary to past ischemic stroke.
2. Left-hand dominant.

Plan
1. Continue current medications as prescribed.
2. Continue physical therapy for mobility and strength.
3. F/u in 3 months for routine check.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, DO, 05/14/2026
explanations: Residual hemiparesis after an ischemic stroke, left dominant side: I69.352 (HCC 253).

distractors.why: Check the documented handedness; when it is not documented, the right side is dominant and the left side non-dominant.
Residual hemiparesis is documented: code the sequela (I69.35-, HCC 253), not Z86.73.
